**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/08 (Sat) 15:33  
[USER] User inquired about examples of companies that have successfully used evaluations to initiate organizational change and improvement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] General Electric (GE) implemented a performance evaluation system called the "Rank and Yank" method in the early 1980s, which required managers to rank employees into three categories and eliminate the bottom 10% each year.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Google uses a performance evaluation system called "Objectives and Key Results" (OKRs) to set specific goals and metrics for employees, improving performance and aligning work with company objectives.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Procter & Gamble (P&G) introduced a performance evaluation system called "Leadership Blueprint," focusing on developing leadership skills through self-assessment tools and development plans.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Toyota employs a performance evaluation system called "Hoshin Kanri," which involves setting strategic goals and cascading them down to departments and individual employees to improve efficiency and productivity.  
[PREFERENCE] User expressed interest in how different companies approach evaluations and use them to drive change.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant noted that each company has a unique approach to evaluations, with the common goal of driving positive change and improvement.  
[PREFERENCE] User found it impressive how companies used evaluations to create positive change and wondered about drawbacks or criticisms of these systems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned criticisms and drawbacks of performance evaluation systems, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Unintended consequences, such as discouraging collaboration or encouraging employees to "game the system."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Biases in performance evaluations based on gender, race, age, or other characteristics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Lack of transparency in the evaluation process, making it difficult for employees to understand how they are judged.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Overemphasis on metrics, which may lead employees to focus on achieving those measures at the expense of other important work aspects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite criticisms, performance evaluation systems can be effective tools for driving positive change when used as part of a larger strategy that includes frequent feedback, coaching, and employee development.
